article_title: InfoQ Counts 64 Commands in Azure's Logic Apps Standard CLI Preview; the Extension's Notes Say 59, and Learn's Command Table Marks Them GA

content_preview.title: InfoQ Counts 64 Commands in Azure's Logic Apps Standard CLI Preview; the Extension's Notes Say 59, and Learn's Command Table Marks Them GA
content_preview.summary: InfoQ reports the logicapp Azure CLI extension preview adds 19 groups and 64 commands; its README and release history say 59, and Microsoft Learn's table marks them GA.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

[InfoQ](https://www.infoq.com/news/2026/11/logic-apps-local-cli/) reports, in an article dated November 12, 2026, that "Microsoft has released a public preview of a local command-line interface for Azure Logic Apps Standard, shipped as the logicapp extension for the Azure CLI." The stated purpose is that a Standard workflow "can be created, run, and tested without Visual Studio Code." editor_notes.content_quality: News, 743 words. The lead says what the CLI is (a local command-line interface for Logic Apps Standard, shipped as the logicapp Azure CLI extension, so that a workflow can be created, run and tested without Visual Studio Code) before turning to the count and status disagreements. A section on what InfoQ describes covers the function (project, workflow, runtime, connector, connection, run and test commands, local host on port 7071, Azurite, runtime doctor, test run) and the limits, so the discrepancy angle does not displace what the tool does. Judged as news: a Microsoft public-preview developer tool reported by InfoQ, where the unusual part is that a developer reading Learn's command table would take the preview commands to be GA; it is a substantive story and not only a documentation curiosity. The 'What the Sources Do Not Say' list keeps the Herald from reconciling the 64 and 59 figures itself.
editor_notes.source_verification: Snapshots read: source-0 (InfoQ, Steef-Jan Wiggers, dated Nov 12, 2026, titled 'Azure Logic Apps Standard Gets a Local CLI in Preview') - confirms every attribution to InfoQ: 'adds 19 command groups with 64 commands beside the thirteen existing cloud-management commands, which it leaves untouched', the runtime doctor and test run quotes, port 7071, Azurite, the three MVPs (Sharma, Gillissen, Panagiotidis, each described as a Microsoft MVP), the limits paragraph and 'Microsoft has said a broader command surface will follow soon'. The MVP commentary is InfoQ's account of LinkedIn posts and the article presents it that way (LinkedIn is not cited). 'Counts' in the headline is faithful: InfoQ states 64 and does not say how it arrived at it. source-6 (README at commit aa52856, fetched raw, sha256 matches the manifest and the current main README): 'The complete extension contributes 59 leaves' and 'Preview Azure CLI extension'; the same file also contains '55-command extension surface' in its testing section (clarification filed). The commit is dated 2026-11-12, after the PR merge, so the 59 is the README's current figure. source-7 (HISTORY.rst): 1.0.0b1 'Contribute the complete 59-command Logic Apps Standard preview'; no 64 anywhere. source-5 (PR #10467, GitHub API confirms merged_at 2026-10-22T00:38:47Z): '59 extension leaves, 21 additions', 'the original 38-command extension', 13 GA core leaves, 'Preview status applies only to this extension's new commands'. source-1 (Learn az logicapp, re-fetched live as well as the snapshot; both identical): I recounted the table myself, 95 data rows = 78 Extension + 16 Core + 1 'Core and Extension' (az logicapp deployment), every one GA. Of the 78 Extension rows, 19 are groups and 59 leaves; of the 16 Core rows, 3 groups and 13 leaves. So the article's '94 rows' is one short (correction filed); 78, 19, 59, 16 and 13 are right. 'Marks them GA' is true of all 59 leaf commands and all 78 extension rows. The page has no preview banner or note: the word 'preview' does not occur in it, and the page metadata shows updated_at 2026-10-22, so the article did not miss a page-level caveat. The 59 leaves and 13 core leaves also match PR #10467 and the README, an independent cross-check of the Herald's counts, and they are labelled the Herald's own in the article. source-2 (Learn extension list, updated 2026-11-02): logicapp, min CLI 2.67.0, Preview, release notes 1.0.0b2; acat is also Preview. source-3 (Learn az logicapp project): 'will automatically install the first time you run an az logicapp project command'; one row, Extension GA. source-4 (Learn az acat report): 17 rows, all Extension GA, as stated. Third-source check: InfoQ's image caption credits the Microsoft Community Hub announcement, which is not on the allowlist and was not fetched (web search unavailable this session); nothing in the allowed sources explains 64, README/PR/HISTORY do not mention 64 anywhere, and the article says so. All 20 quoted strings were checked verbatim against the cited page they are attributed to (script-normalised for curly quotes and whitespace): 20 of 20 found. Allowlist: all 8 hosts already allowed, no additions. Prompt-injection scan: suspicious_patterns null for all 8 sources, nothing to judge. Independence: one independent outlet (InfoQ); everything else is Microsoft or the extension's own repository; News needs only that sources be reputable and the article does not claim more. Anthropic disclosure: not required - Anthropic and its products are not in the story.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Headline, summary and lead are each backed. 'InfoQ Counts 64' is InfoQ's wording; 'the Extension's Notes Say 59' is the README and HISTORY (59 leaves, 59-command), the summary names them as 'README and release history'; 'Learn's Command Table Marks Them GA' is true of the command table and the article states in the body that the extension list says Preview. 'Them' is unambiguous in the summary (the extension's commands). Two subordinate issues: the row total (94, actual 95; the omitted row is the Core and Extension deployment group) and the unmentioned '55-command extension surface' in the README. Absence claims tested: 'None of the other cited pages gives 64' (no 64 in the Learn pages, PR, README or HISTORY other than 64-bit/64-KiB), 'None of the cited sources gives a general-availability date' (none found), 'InfoQ does not say how it arrived at 64' (true). Dates: Nov 12 (InfoQ), 2026-10-22 00:38 UTC (merge, with time basis stated), Nov 13 recount.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral. The Herald declines to reconcile the figures and labels its own counts as its own.
editor_notes.originality: No earlier Herald article covers the Logic Apps Standard CLI; checked src/content/articles for logicapp and Logic Apps.
concerns: Row total stated as 94; the Learn table has 95 rows (one typed Core and Extension). Filed as a correction.
README's second figure, '55-command extension surface', is not mentioned; filed as a clarification.
The headline is long (138 characters, within the 150 limit) and compressed, but accurate on each of its three clauses.
recommendations: When counting table rows by type, list every Type value present and reconcile the sum to the total before publishing.
When quoting a count from a document, search the same document for other counts of the same thing.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Substantively sound and honestly framed: every InfoQ attribution, all 20 quotes and the Herald's own 78/19/59/13 counts check out against raw source text, and the Learn page carries no preview banner the article missed. The only defects are subordinate (a row total off by one and an unmentioned second README figure), covered by a corrections record. Featured candidacy: 1 - solid for a defined developer audience (Azure Logic Apps developers and anyone reading Learn's status column), narrow reach.
